faq.q: Is our data used to train AI models?
faq.a: No. With the commercial APIs we use (Anthropic, OpenAI), your data is not used for training by default. For sensitive data we run open-source models on our own servers or yours, so nothing leaves that environment.

faq.q: What does the EU AI Act mean for these automations?
faq.a: Most business automations — content drafts, lead routing, document processing — fall into the low-risk categories. The main duties are transparency (for example, telling people when they are talking to an AI agent) and keeping a person in control. We build both in and document every workflow; for a formal legal assessment, please talk to your lawyer.

faq.q: Can we use AI without sending data to OpenAI or Anthropic?
faq.a: Yes. We host open-source models on our own hardware or on your infrastructure. They work well for document processing, internal search and assistants; for the most demanding writing, the large cloud models are still ahead, and we tell you where the trade-off lies.

faq.q: What if the AI gets something wrong?
faq.a: That is why every workflow has a human checkpoint. Nothing customer-facing goes live without someone on your team or ours approving it, and we tune prompts and rules as errors show up.

faq.q: Do we have to change our tools?
faq.a: Usually not. We connect to the shop, CRM, inbox and spreadsheets you already use. If a tool has no API, we tell you up front.
You do. Workflows run in accounts in your name where possible, and every one is documented and handed over.

faq.q: How long does a first automation take?
faq.a: A focused automation is typically live within two to four weeks: one week of discovery, one to two weeks for a prototype on real data, then a short pilot.

faq.q: Which processes are a bad fit for AI?
faq.a: Tasks that happen rarely, need judgement on every single case, or where one mistake is very expensive. We’ll say so in the opportunity check rather than build something you don’t need.
